Saturation vapour pressure

Source: R/forcing-derived.R
ef_es.Rd

Computes the saturation vapour pressure \(e^\circ(T)\) at a given air temperature with the FAO-56 equation.

Usage

ef_es(air_temperature)

Arguments

air_temperature

Numeric. Air temperature \(T\) [degrees Celsius]. Must be finite and > -237.3, where the equation is defined.

Value

A numeric vector of saturation vapour pressure [kPa] with the length of air_temperature, keeping its dim.

Details

$$e^\circ(T) = 0.6108 \exp\left(\frac{17.27\,T}{T + 237.3}\right)$$ (FAO-56, chapter 3, Eq. 11).

Mean saturation vapour pressure. For periods of one day or longer the saturation vapour pressure of the period is the mean of the values at the daily maximum and minimum temperatures (FAO-56, Eq. 12): (ef_es(tmax) + ef_es(tmin)) / 2. Using the mean temperature instead underestimates it and the reference evapotranspiration (FAO-56, chapter 3 and box 7). For hourly periods, ef_es() of the hourly mean temperature is used (FAO-56, Eq. 53). The vapour pressure deficit is the difference between this value and the actual vapour pressure (ef_ea_daily() and related functions).

Temperatures are in degrees Celsius (decision WF-02): a temperature passed in kelvin (for example 293) gives a meaningless value and is not detected here (it is a quality-control matter, flag EF_WS_IMPLAUSIBLE, not registered).

Missing values propagate. Non-numeric or empty input raises earthflux_input_error; temperatures <= -237.3 or infinite raise earthflux_domain_error.

Verification status

VERIFICADA (FAO-56, chapter 3, Eqs. 11 and 12; case V2: e°(24.5) = 3.075 kPa, e°(15) = 1.705 kPa). FAO-56 annex 3, Eq. 3-8 uses 0.611 instead of 0.6108; the chapter 3 form is adopted (dev/specs/weather-forcing.md 4.3). The same function and the same daily mean (Tmax and Tmin) and hourly forms are ASCE-EWRI (2005) Eqs. 6-7 (p. 11) and Eq. 37 (p. 29).

References

Allen, R. G., Pereira, L. S., Raes, D., & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration: Guidelines for computing crop water requirements (FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56). FAO, Rome. ISBN 92-5-104219-5.

ASCE-EWRI (2005). The ASCE Standardized Reference Evapotranspiration Equation. Task Committee on Standardization of Reference Evapotranspiration, Environmental and Water Resources Institute of the American Society of Civil Engineers. Final report, January 2005. Published as Allen, R. G., Walter, I. A., Elliott, R. L., Howell, T. A., Itenfisu, D., Jensen, M. E., & Snyder, R. L. (Eds.), American Society of Civil Engineers, Reston, VA. doi:10.1061/9780784408056

See also

Other derived meteorological variables: ef_dewpoint(), ef_ea, ef_es_slope(), ef_psychrometric(), ef_ra_daily(), ef_ra_period(), ef_rso(), ef_wind_2m()

Examples

# FAO-56 example 3: Tmax = 24.5 and Tmin = 15 degrees C
ef_es(c(24.5, 15))
#> [1] 3.074649 1.705346
# Mean saturation vapour pressure of the day (Eq. 12)
mean(ef_es(c(24.5, 15)))
#> [1] 2.389998
